title: LabOS System Architecture
note: One central LabOS server hosts scientific AI reasoning, specialist sub-agents, knowledge and memory, and deterministic coordination. A server-side model router prefers a remote cloud model and falls back to the server's local LLM when cloud connectivity, the API or its quota is unavailable. The agents preserve experiment context and tool permissions across model changes. Each instrument-host PC runs one persistent execution worker, called a PC Agent. The worker does not require a local large language model. It owns instrument sessions, bounded adapters, a command journal, watchdog and artifact outbox. An operator computer can use only a browser. All laboratory PCs initiate their HTTP(S) connections; command arrows represent payload flow, not inbound network sessions. Physical device interfaces remain local to the instrument host. A/B retain the supplied optical and sample-lab inventory; C through N illustrate additional resource hosts. Hardware reference and trigger cables are separate from this control network. This figure describes the scalable LabOS system design, rather than an inventory of currently commissioned drivers.
source: Original LabOS architecture drawing, based on project design and the supplied laboratory scenario.
